_meta.comment: Status: design draft for review - decided, built where served. This file is the normative machine shape of the MCP tool catalog declared in mcp-plugin.md: exactly the tools/list result payload the server serves, the three tools oml_write, oml_read and oml_workarea (ADR-0039 d2), each with its MCP annotations (d5). It declares only what is served: a served tool's entry changes only in the same change as the code that serves it, so the server never advertises a field it refuses. The designed tools and the served tools' designed arguments live in mcp-tools.designed.json, which is never served and names no tool this file names (scripts/check_contract_sync.py). pending_design names, per served tool, what mcp-plugin.md decides that the build does not carry yet. Target MCP specification revision: 2025-06-18 (streamable HTTP transport, run stateless per mcp-plugin.md).
_meta.output_shapes: This file declares inputSchemas only. Tool OUTPUT shapes are deliberately prose-normative in mcp-plugin.md until the implementation pins structured output schemas.

pending_design.oml_read: ADR-0039 d4 and ADR-0013 d1, d2, ADR-0025 d9: the lineage mode's lineage and depth are designed (mcp-tools.designed.json) and refused with request.validation naming the field until the lineage read is routed. mcp-plugin.md decides hybrid FTS + vector as the only search mode and logs every recall to the read log; the build serves full-text search alone (vector search waits on RS-1) and computes the ids served and the query_digest on every recall, which no read log records yet.
pending_design.oml_write: ADR-0039 d2, d9: attachments is designed (mcp-tools.designed.json), naming upload sessions made outside MCP, and is refused with request.validation as outside the input schema until uploads are built.

tools.name: oml_write
tools.description: Store a claim, a claim derived from others, a new version of one, or a proposal to retire one. Held on arrival: scanned same-call, then reviewed by an identity that did not write it, visible to others only after ratification. Without replaces it is a submission on POST /v1/memories, journalled learn when derives_from is non-empty and remember otherwise; with replaces it supersedes that version on POST /v1/memories/{artifact_id}/supersede. A field outside the chosen mode is refused with request.validation naming it in details.field, never dropped.

text.description: The claim text, or, with retirement true, why the claim is retired. At most submission.max_body_size (shipped 1 MiB) UTF-8 bytes of the NFC-normalized text; larger is refused with request.payload_too_large.

idempotency_key.description: Without replaces it is scoped to (key, resolved workarea), as a submission's; with replaces to the calling key alone, whatever the target's workarea, as a supersession's. Within one scope, a retry with the same key and an identical request returns the stored response with idempotent_replay true, and the same key with a different request is a typed error, never a second write (D13). The same key reused across the two modes, or on two submissions into different workareas, is a separate write.

claim_key.description: Groups the versions of one claim. Omitted, the server derives auto- plus 16 hex digits from the key and the text, and a sent key starting auto- is refused. Refused with replaces: the new version takes its target's.

kind.description: The claim's kind; omitted, memory, or with replaces the target's. With replaces only memory, derived_fact and steering are accepted, within the kind-change rule (docs/architecture/audit-and-lineage.md).

derives_from.description: Artifact ids this claim derives from, each readable by the key; non-empty, a submission is journalled learn. With replaces the target is included implicitly.

anchor.description: Where the memory came from, as you read it: {repo, rev, path, fragment?, hash?, hasher?} for a file in a git repository (repo like github.com/owner/name, rev the full commit id, path relative, fragment a heading slug, a decision handle such as d3, or a line span such as L10-L42), or {uri, rev?, fragment?} for a web page. The reviewer sees it beside the text; it is signed with the version and never changes. A successor declares its own; nothing is inherited.

workarea.description: The workarea, by node id or name. Without replaces, the workarea written in, omitted the key's default. With replaces it must be the target's workarea.

replaces.description: The artifact id of the claim's current served tip to supersede (submission.tip_conflict otherwise). A target of a vocabulary kind (term, term_mapping, vocab_release) is refused; supersede it on the HTTP API.

expected_version.description: With replaces, required: the claim's latest version as you last read it (the version field of the tip you are replacing, or of your own newer held version). If the claim has moved on, the write is refused with submission.version_conflict and details.current_version; read it again before retrying.

retirement.description: With replaces, true proposes retiring the claim: once a non-author ratifies, recall stops serving it and every version stays readable. Refused without replaces.

reason.description: With replaces, the reason for the change. Refused without replaces.

valid_from.description: When the claim holds in the world, as its author declares it: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, or an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset; a period names its first instant, so 2015 begins 1 January 2015; a period is read in UTC. Signed with the claim and never changed; a new version states its own. Only memory and derived_fact take it.

valid_until.description: When the claim stops holding: the same forms as valid_from, a period naming its whole span, so valid_until 2015 holds through 31 December 2015 and a day holds through that day. A recall hides a claim whose valid_until has passed unless include_expired is true. To end a fact, supersede it with valid_until set; the server never ends one itself.

tools.name: oml_read
tools.description: Search the team's reviewed memory for facts, decisions and known pitfalls before non-trivial work, on a project term you do not know, and after a failed command: pass query with the words a note would use, or a question, such as an identifier, an error code, a module or a file name; any word may match, an identifier matches by its parts and a word by its stem, rows holding more of the words rank higher, each hit's matched lists the words it holds, and a recall that finds little offers did_you_mean spellings, so try other words before concluding nothing is stored. Find, fetch or list claims; the fields present choose the mode. artifact_id fetches one version (GET /v1/memories/{artifact_id}): the calling key's own rows in any state, others' promoted versions within read access, anything else access.not_found. query recalls (POST /v1/memories/recall): promoted claims in a workarea subtree, steering first and never ranked or cut by max_tokens, and with include_unreviewed the key's own held rows flagged state held. Neither lists (GET /v1/memories): own true, the default, is everything the key wrote, newest first, in any state, so state tells an agent whether its write was approved or rejected; own false is the promoted tips of a workarea. An argument outside the chosen mode, or artifact_id and query together, is refused with request.validation naming it in details.field. Every mode answers claim items with their text under mode: get, recall or listing. A recall also answers recall_id; on your next read, in any mode, feedback names which of its hits answered the question and which did not.

artifact_id.description: Get mode: the version to read; each version of a claim has its own artifact_id, and superseded versions stay readable as history. Refused beside query.

query.description: Recall mode: the search text, ranked by the search pipeline that search names, or by the tenant's default.

workarea.description: Recall and listing: the subtree read, by node id or name. Omitted, recall and the listing with own false read the key's default workarea (request.workarea_unresolved for a key with none), and the listing with own true every workarea the key wrote in. A node the key may not be told about answers access.not_found, indistinguishable from a nonexistent node.

k.description: Recall: how many hits to return, at most 100 as on the ring.

kinds.description: Recall: the hit kinds served; an empty array is refused, so only an absent kinds means no filter. Steering is never a hit.

anchor_repo.description: Recall and listing: only claims whose anchor names this repository (github.com/owner/name); unanchored claims are left out. Refused in get mode.

anchor_path_prefix.description: Recall and listing: only claims whose anchor path starts with this prefix, such as docs/adr/ or src/store.rs; unanchored claims are left out. Refused in get mode.

include_unreviewed.description: Recall, default false. True: the calling key's own held rows that match (kind memory or derived_fact, never steering or retirement versions) join the hits, ranked in the same order and flagged state held; they count against k and max_tokens.

max_tokens.description: Recall: a budget in budget tokens (counter oml-tc/1, not a model's count), at most 2^53 - 1 as on the ring. Steering is never cut; the hits served are the longest rank prefix that fits, and budget reports the cut.

search.description: Recall: the search pipeline, among those the server serves (configuration search.enabled); omitted, the tenant's default, else the deployment's. keyword-all needs every word exactly; keyword-any takes any word; bm25 adds identifier parts, stems and rarity weights; bm25-trigram fuses bm25 with trigram similarity for misspellings and fragments; bm25-postings ranks as bm25 from an index, leaving out words frequent among the memories the key reads (named in search.pruned) and still scoring them; bm25-rerank reorders bm25's best candidates with a local cross-encoder, each hit's matched.rerank its relevance, and where the server sets a relevance floor it answers no hit when nothing passes, saying how many it withheld in search.below_floor; sparse ranks by a learned sparse model's token weights, matching related words the memory does not say, and bm25-sparse fuses it with bm25-postings, each hit's matched.tokens naming the tokens that scored it and matched.expanded the ones the model added. bm25-postings-time adds the memories whose declared valid time overlaps a date the query names (in 2015, last week, since March 2025, read by rule and shown in search.window), ranked by reciprocal rank beside bm25-postings. A name the server does not serve is refused with request.validation naming /search; the answer's search.pipeline names the one that ran.

match.description: Recall, default any. all: only rows holding every query word are hits; when none does, the any-word hits are served and search.fallback says any_term.

include_expired.description: Recall, default false. True also serves claims whose valid_until has passed, which recall hides by default; get and the listing always serve them.

now.description: Recall: the instant the recall is read at, YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD or an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset; omitted, the server's clock; relative dates are counted in UTC days. It decides which claims have expired and anchors the query's relative dates such as last week.

own.description: Listing, default true: the calling key's own submissions in every state. False: the promoted served tips of the workarea's subtree within the key's read access.

claim_key.description: Listing: the versions of one claim.

state.description: Listing: a state filter. Over the key's own work, promoted says a write was approved and rejected that it was not.

since.description: Listing: versions written at or after this RFC 3339 date-time (inclusive).

until.description: Listing: versions written before this RFC 3339 date-time (exclusive).

limit.description: Listing: page size, at most 200 as on the ring.

cursor.description: Listing: the opaque next_cursor of the previous page; the client holds it (stateless).

recall_id.description: The recall_id of this key's recall, in the last 24 hours, that the feedback is about.

useful.description: Hits of that recall that answered the question.

not_useful.description: Hits of that recall that did not.

feedback.description: Any mode. Which hits of this key's last recall answered its question and which did not, at most 20 ids, each a hit that recall served; checked before the read runs, refused by field, and never changes what this read answers. Recall improves for the next reader from it.

tools.name: oml_workarea
tools.description: One workarea as the calling key is allowed to see it: identity, derived path, status, crew record, readable immediate children, the verbs this key's effective access carries there with the permission epoch, the review policy in force, the status proposals waiting for a second identity, and the workarea's brief: the claims its reviewers agreed an agent entering it reads first, as claim items with their text, within the brief's token budget. Rides GET /v2/workareas/{workarea}, one call.

workarea.description: Optional workarea, by node id or name. Omitted: the key's default workarea; a key with none is refused (request.workarea_unresolved).
